newHelpers.title: Entropy bounds for a finite mixture of states
newHelpers.statement:
For states $\rho_i$ and finite probabilities $p_i$, put $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$. Then
$$0\le S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\le H(p).$$
newHelpers.proof:
Omit zero weights. Positivity of $\bar\rho-p_i\rho_i$ implies $\ker\bar\rho\subseteq\ker\rho_i$ (take its quadratic form on a kernel vector), so every relative entropy below is finite. Expanding the spectral cross traces gives
$$S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)=\sum_i p_iD(\rho_i\Vert\bar\rho)\ge0$$
by the actual finite-state QRE nonnegativity supplier. For the upper bound, diagonalize each $\rho_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}|v_{ij}\rangle\langle v_{ij}|$, omitting zero eigenvalues, and purify the mixture as $|v\rangle=\sum_{ij}\sqrt{p_i\lambda_{ij}}|v_{ij}\rangle\otimes|i,j\rangle$. Its label marginal $G$ has diagonal $q_{ij}=p_i\lambda_{ij}$ and has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\bar\rho$ by Schmidt decomposition. For $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(q)$, positivity gives $\operatorname{supp}G\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\Delta$; hence
$$0\le D(G\Vert\Delta)=H(q)-S(G)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)-S(\bar\rho).$$
This proves both bounds, including singleton/zero-weight cases.

newHelpers.title: Dimension-dependent quantum entropy continuity and Holevo control
newHelpers.statement: Write $h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ with continuous endpoints. Let $g(t)=(1+t)\ln(1+t)-t\ln t$ for $t\in[0,1]$, with $g(0)=0$. For states $\rho,\sigma$ on dimension $d\ge1$ and $t=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, $$|S(\rho)-S(\sigma)|\le t\ln d+g(t).$$ Moreover, if $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_M$ are states on that space and $a=M^{-1}\sum_m\frac12\|\sigma_m-\sigma\|_1$, their uniform Holevo information is at most $2a\ln d+2g(a)$. In particular on dimension $d_E^n$, exponential decay of $a$ makes unnormalized Holevo information tend to zero.
newHelpers.proof:
If $t=0$, equality of the states settles the claim. Otherwise the positive and negative parts of $\rho-\sigma$ have trace $t$, because that difference has trace zero. Normalize them to states $\omega_+,\omega_-$. Then
$$\theta=\frac{\rho+t\omega_-}{1+t}=\frac{\sigma+t\omega_+}{1+t}.$$
Apply the lower mixture-entropy bound to the first representation and upper bound to the second. After multiplication by $1+t$ this gives
$$S(\rho)-S(\sigma)\le t\bigl[S(\omega_+)-S(\omega_-)\bigr]+(1+t)h(t/(1+t))\le t\ln d+g(t).$$
Interchanging the states gives the absolute-value bound. Dimension one causes no exception. The function $g$ is increasing and concave: for $t>0$, $g'(t)=\ln(1+1/t)>0$ and $g''(t)=-1/[t(1+t)]<0$; continuity extends Jensen to $t=0$.

Consequently, if states $\sigma_m$ on dimension $d$ have average half-distance $a=M^{-1}\sum_m T(\sigma_m,\sigma)$ from one target state $\sigma$, then their uniform Holevo information satisfies
$$\chi(\{M^{-1},\sigma_m\})\le2a\ln d+2g(a).$$
Indeed the average state is within $a$ by the triangle inequality; apply the entropy-continuity estimate to its entropy and to the average of the individual entropies, and use Jensen for $g$. This is a proved quantitative implication for this particular finite ensemble, not an identification of secrecy metrics. When $d=d_E^n$ and $a$ decays exponentially, the unnormalized Holevo information tends to zero.

newHelpers.title: Exponential averaged spectral projectors for a finite cq ensemble
newHelpers.statement:
For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.
newHelpers.proof:
For $P_n$, retain product eigenvectors of $\bar\rho^{\otimes n}$ whose positive eigenvalue has negative logarithm in $n[S(\bar\rho)-\eta,S(\bar\rho)+\eta]$. For $Q_{x^n}$, use product eigenvectors of $\rho_{x^n}=\bigotimes_i\rho_{x_i}$ whose eigenvalue has negative logarithm in $n[s-\eta,s+\eta]$. The upper eigenvalue bounds are immediate. The lower retained eigenvalue and trace at most one imply each rank bound. Under the joint law $\Pr(X=x,J=j)=p_x\lambda_{xj}$, with zero-probability eigenvalues omitted, the random variable $Z=-\ln\lambda_{XJ}$ has finite support and mean $s$. Its IID sum controls the second failure probability exactly. The first failure is the same argument for the spectral law of $\bar\rho$; averaging inputs gives $\bar\rho^{\otimes n}$.

For completeness, a finite supported centered variable $Y$ with $|Y|\le b$ obeys $\mathbb E e^{uY}\le1+u^2b^2e^{|u|b}/2$, by the Taylor remainder and $\mathbb EY=0$. For small fixed $u>0$, $\ln\mathbb E e^{uY}<u\eta/2$. Markov's inequality and independence then bound $\Pr(\sum Y_i\ge n\eta)\le e^{-nu\eta/2}$; apply the same argument to $-Y$ and add. A constant spectral variable has zero failure probability and needs no division by a range. All logarithms are evaluated only on positive-probability eigenvalues.

newHelpers.title: Exact flat spectral-type reduction of channel information
newHelpers.statement: Let $\rho$ be a state on dimension $d$ and $\mathcal N$ a finite-dimensional channel. There is an exact decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t$ into mutually orthogonal flat spectral-type states, with at most $(n+1)^d$ positive-weight types and $H(T)\le d\ln(n+1)$. For its fixed complementary channel, $$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$ $$\sum_t p_t[S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})]\ge n[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]-2H(T).$$ Thus in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound.
newHelpers.proof:
Let $\rho=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j|j\rangle\langle j|$. The product $\rho^{\otimes n}$ decomposes as
$$\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t,$$
where $t$ ranges over its positive-probability spectral types and $\tau_t$ is the uniform state on that type subspace. There are at most $(n+1)^d$ such types; their supports are orthogonal. Thus
$$\sum_t p_tS(\tau_t)=nS(\rho)-H(T),\quad H(T)\le d\ln(n+1).$$
For any fixed channel $\mathcal N$ with complement $\mathcal N^c$, the mixture bounds applied separately to their outputs yield
$$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$
$$\sum_t p_t\{S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\}\ge n\{S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\}-2H(T).$$
Indeed the averaged receiver entropy is at least its mixture entropy minus $H(T)$; averaged environment entropy is at most its mixture entropy. The input entropy identity follows directly by summing eigenvalues over disjoint type blocks. Therefore in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound. These are exact finite-$n$ estimates; no replacement of fixed-dimensional continuity by a uniform bound is involved.

newHelpers.title: Finite unitary averaging and a decoupling second-moment bound
newHelpers.statement:
Let $D\ge2$, $1\le K\le D$, and $\omega_{AE}\succeq0$ with $\dim A=D$, $\operatorname{tr}\omega\le1$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}\omega_E$. For every $\delta>0$ there is an explicitly specified finite probability ensemble of isometries $W:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^D$ such that, for
$$\omega^W_{RE}=\frac DK(W^T\otimes I_E)\omega_{AE}(\overline W\otimes I_E),$$
one has
$$\mathbb E\left\|\omega^W_{RE}-\frac{I_R}{K}\otimes\omega_E\right\|_1\le\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{AE}^2)}+\delta.$$
At the same time the ensemble can be required to satisfy, for every Hermitian $Z_{AE}$,
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac DK(W^T\otimes I)Z(\overline W\otimes I)\right\|_1\le(1+\delta)\|Z\|_1.$$
No Haar existence or Gaussian-law supplier, and no choice axiom, is used.
newHelpers.proof:
Let $G$ be the finite group of monomial unitaries whose nonzero entries are fifth roots of unity. Let $R$ be the real rotation by $\pi/4$ in coordinates 1 and 2, acting identically elsewhere. Use the symmetric finite list $\mathcal S=G\cup\{R,R^*\}$, retaining multiplicities if any. At each walk step choose the identity with probability $1/2$ and an element of this list uniformly with the remaining probability. For $j=1,2$, the moment operator on matrices is
$$T_j(X)=\tfrac12X+\frac1{2|\mathcal S|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal S}U^{\otimes j}X(U^*)^{\otimes j}.$$
These are self-adjoint contractions for the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, because the list is inverse-symmetric; laziness makes every eigenvalue nonnegative. Moreover
$$\langle X,(I-T_j)X\rangle=\frac1{4|\mathcal S|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal S}\|X-U^{\otimes j}X(U^*)^{\otimes j}\|_2^2.$$
Thus their fixed spaces are exactly the simultaneous commutants of the displayed finite unitaries.

For $j=1$, the independent diagonal fifth-root phases force a commuting matrix to be diagonal; permutations force all its diagonal entries equal. For $j=2$, a matrix coefficient from $|i,j\rangle$ to $|k,l\rangle$ can survive the diagonal phases only when the unordered multisets $\{i,j\}$ and $\{k,l\}$ agree. Indeed each index occurs with multiplicity 0, 1 or 2; equality modulo 5 of every exponent forces equality of these integer multiplicities. Commutation with all permutations then leaves three constants: $c$ on $|i,i\rangle$, $a$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle i,j|$ for $i\ne j$, and $b$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle j,i|$. Commutation with $R\otimes R$ applied to $|1,1\rangle$, whose rotated vector has nonzero coefficients on both $|1,2\rangle$ and $|2,1\rangle$, forces $c=a+b$. Conversely $I$ and the swap $F$ commute with every tensor-square unitary. The fixed space is therefore precisely $\operatorname{span}\{I,F\}$, also when $D=2$.

Finite-dimensional spectral decomposition now gives orthogonal projections $\mathcal P_1,\mathcal P_2$ onto these fixed spaces and a number $0\le\lambda<1$ such that
$$\|T_j^L-\mathcal P_j\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda^L,\qquad j=1,2.$$
If the orthogonal complement is zero, take its spectral radius as zero. Every $T_j^L$ is the moment of an actual finite distribution of length-$L$ unitary words; the limit is only a finite-matrix spectral calculation, not an assumed Haar integral. The first projection is $\mathcal P_1(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X)I/D$. For any rank-$K$ projection $P_0$, invariance of trace and swap trace gives
$$\mathcal P_2(P_0\otimes P_0)=a_0I+b_0F,\qquad a_0=\frac{K(KD-1)}{D(D^2-1)},\quad b_0=\frac{K(D-K)}{D(D^2-1)}.$$
The coefficients solve $a_0D^2+b_0D=K^2$ and $a_0D+b_0D^2=K$.

Choose a coordinate isometry $W_0$ and let $W=UW_0$, where $U$ is a finite walk word. Complex conjugation preserves the same limiting first and second moment projections and their norm bounds, so they apply to $P=\overline W W^T$ as well. The swap identity on matrix units gives the following limiting second moment, with $\Omega=I_R/K\otimes\omega_E$:
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2
=\frac{D(KD-1)}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+\frac{1-DK}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)
\le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2).$$
In detail, the squared-state term is $(D^2/K^2)\{a_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+b_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)\}$, and the limiting mean is $\Omega$, so subtract $\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)/K$.

The finite moment error has a quantitative bound. Put $d_E=\dim E$ and $\varepsilon=\lambda^L$. The first-moment error in each matrix unit of the compressed reference is at most $\varepsilon$ in Hilbert–Schmidt norm; contracting it with $\omega$ shows $\|\mathbb E\omega^W-\Omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon\|\omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon$. For the squared-state term, the second-moment error on $P_0\otimes P_0$ has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $K\varepsilon$. In its trace pairing with $F_E(\omega\otimes\omega)$, the partial trace over the two environment copies has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $d_E\|\omega\|_2^2\le d_E$ (Cauchy–Schwarz for each diagonal block). Consequently that squared-state error is at most $D^2d_E\varepsilon/K$. The cross term with $\Omega$, whose Hilbert–Schmidt norm is at most $1/\sqrt K$, has error at most $2D\varepsilon/\sqrt K$. Hence, with $C_D=D^2d_E+2D$,
$$\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2\le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+C_D\varepsilon.$$
Positivity implies $\operatorname{supp}\omega\subseteq A\otimes\operatorname{supp}\omega_E$: a kernel vector of the marginal has a sum of nonnegative diagonal quadratic forms equal to zero, forcing the corresponding rows and columns to vanish. Thus each difference has rank at most $Kr$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen give the trace-norm bound at most $\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)}+\sqrt{KrC_D\varepsilon}$.

Finally write a Hermitian $Z$ as $Z_+-Z_-$. Positivity of compression bounds its trace norm by the two positive compressed traces. The first-moment bound $\|\mathbb EP-(K/D)I\|_\infty\le\sqrt K\varepsilon$ gives
$$\mathbb E\|\mathcal C_W(Z)\|_1\le(1+D\varepsilon/\sqrt K)\|Z\|_1.$$
Choose a finite $L$ with both $KrC_D\lambda^L\le\delta^2$ and $D\lambda^L/\sqrt K\le\delta$. Such an integer exists by $\lambda<1$; the least such integer is a specified choice. If $r=0$, the positive operator is zero and its decoupling bound is automatic. This proves both assertions with an actual finite ensemble and exact dimension-dependent moment control.

newHelpers.title: Flat-input coherent information is achievable by subspace codes
newHelpers.statement: Let $V:\mathbb C^d\to B\otimes E$ be a Stinespring isometry and $\tau=I_d/d$. Every $0<R<I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable by isometric subspace entanglement transmission. If the coherent information is nonpositive, the lower bound is supplied by the one-dimensional code. Here an $n$-use code has an isometry $W_n:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a CPTP decoder to $\mathbb C^{K_n}$; its squared overlap with the maximally entangled target tends to one and $n^{-1}\ln K_n\to R$. The same conclusion holds for a flat state on any nonzero input subspace by composing with its embedding.
newHelpers.proof:
Set $s_B=S(\mathcal N(\tau))$, $s_E=S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$. Choose $\eta>0$ with $R<s_B-s_E-2\eta$. On $n$ uses, let $|v_n\rangle=(I\otimes V^{\otimes n})|\Phi_{d^n}\rangle$ in factor order $A'B^nE^n$. Let $P_n,Q_n$ be the spectral projectors for the IID receiver and environment states from finite-estimates.md, and let $\epsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bound the sum of their failure probabilities. The commuting joint projection has acceptance at least $1-\epsilon_n$. For
$$|\widehat v_n\rangle=(I_{A'}\otimes P_n\otimes Q_n)|v_n\rangle,$$
the rank-two pure-vector calculation used in gentle measurement gives
$$\bigl\||v_n\rangle\langle v_n|-|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|\bigr\|_1\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}.$$
This follows also by applying the actual gentle-measurement lemma to the pure state and the joint projection. Let $\omega=\operatorname{Tr}_{B^n}|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|$. Its environment rank is at most $e^{n(s_E+\eta)}$. Since the projected vector is pure,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{B^n}^2).$$
Moreover
$$0\preceq\omega_{B^n}\preceq P_n\mathcal N(\tau)^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}P_n.$$
To verify the first inequality, take the partial trace after $Q_n$; the complementary environment projection produces another positive summand of the original receiver marginal. Hence $\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)\le e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}$, because its trace is at most one.

Take $K_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$. It is at most $d^n$: subadditivity on the pure Stinespring output implies $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$. If $I_c>0$ then $d\ge2$. For an isometry $W:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n}$, let $\rho^W_{RE^n}$ be the environment/reference state produced by encoding half of $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle$. Coefficient matrices give exactly the normalized-compression expression for the unprojected marginal. Use the finite ensemble above with tolerance $e^{-n}$. Apply its compression estimate to $\omega$, and its averaged trace-contraction estimate to the difference between projected and unprojected marginals. Their environment marginals differ by at most $2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}$. The triangle inequality therefore yields
$$\mathbb E\left\|\rho^W_{RE^n}-\frac{I_R}{K_n}\otimes\mathcal N^c(\tau)^{\otimes n}\right\|_1
\le6\sqrt{\epsilon_n}+2e^{-n}+\sqrt{2e^{-n(s_B-s_E-R-2\eta)}}\longrightarrow0.$$
Order the finite generator list and its length-$L$ words. For each $n$, take the first word whose displayed norm is at most twice its expectation; if that expectation is zero, take the first zero-norm word. A qualifying word exists by finite averaging. This specifies the entire encoder sequence without countable choices.

The product target is purified by $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle_{RM}\otimes|e_n\rangle_{E^nF}$, with a sufficiently large finite $F$. The actual encoded Stinespring output is another purification on reference/environment versus receiver. Root-fidelity purification characterization, after adding a pure finite ancilla to the receiver if needed, supplies an isometry on the receiver's purifying space whose overlap with that target is the root fidelity of the two marginals. The fixed-purification form follows from the published purification/unitary-equivalence theorem. Fuchs–van de Graaf makes this root fidelity at least one minus half the displayed norm. Trace out the extra decoder factor $F$: the resulting CPTP decoder has squared entanglement fidelity at least the square of that overlap and hence tending to one. The encoder is exactly the isometry $W$; no generating-code/transmitting-code equivalence is assumed. Fix ordered bases throughout. In the purification characterization use the polar/SVD attaining map, extending every kernel partial isometry by the ordered basis completion; in repeated eigenspaces, project the ordered coordinate vectors and Gram–Schmidt in that order. This specifies a decoder at each block length by one formula, rather than choosing a sequence of unrelated attaining maps.

newHelpers.title: Finite cq wiretap achievability with strong Holevo secrecy
newHelpers.statement: Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.
newHelpers.proof:
Choose $r$with $\chi_E<r$ and $R+r<\chi_B$, and then choose $\eta>0$ so $r>\chi_E+2\eta$ and $R+r<\chi_B-2\eta$. Take $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nr}\rceil$ and draw $M_nL_n$ independent words $X^n(m,l)$ with law $p^{\otimes n}$. For message $m$, the encoder inputs the mixed state
$$\rho_{m,n}=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{l=1}^{L_n}\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\rho_{X_i(m,l)}.$$
This is a legitimate finite private randomization of the operational input state; the realized codebook is public.

For Bob use the global and conditional spectral projectors $P,Q_{x^n}$ from finite-estimates.md, for the receiver ensemble. Put $\Gamma_{m,l}=P Q_{X^n(m,l)}P$, form the square-root POVM from all $\Gamma_{m,l}$, and assign its kernel/failure outcome to one message. The existing finite Hayashi–Nagaoka operator inequality bounds each pair-decoding error by twice its own projector failure plus four times its interference sum. The estimate is valid without a uniform per-word projector-acceptance hypothesis: only its average is needed here. Specifically,
$$\mathbb E[1-\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_{m,l}\beta_{X^n(m,l)})]\le\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n},$$
where $\varepsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bounds both averaged projector failures. This follows by $\operatorname{tr}(Q_xP\beta_xP)\ge\operatorname{tr}(Q_x\beta_x)-\|P\beta_xP-\beta_x\|_1$ and the actual gentle-measurement bound followed by Jensen. For two different independent codewords, the spectral eigenvalue and rank bounds give
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\beta_{X_i^n})
=\operatorname{tr}[(P\mathbb E Q_{X_j^n}P)(P\bar\beta^{\otimes n}P)]
\le e^{-n(S(\bar\beta)-\eta)}e^{n(\sum_xp_xS(\beta_x)+\eta)}
=e^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)}.$$
The equality uses the support of the first factor; the inequality uses positivity of the operator-order difference, not commutation of the two factors. Thus expected pair-error is at most
$$2(\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n})+4M_nL_ne^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)},$$
which decays exponentially. Coarsening the pair POVM to its message label cannot increase message error.

For Eve let $P,Q_{x^n}$ denote the spectral projectors for her ensemble, put $s_E=\sum_xp_xS(\epsilon_x)$, and define
$$\xi_{x^n}=P Q_{x^n}\epsilon_{x^n}Q_{x^n}P,\qquad\theta=\mathbb E\xi_{X^n}.$$
These operators satisfy $0\preceq\xi_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}P$, $\operatorname{tr}\xi_{x^n}\le1$, and $\operatorname{rank}P\le e^{n(S(\bar\epsilon)+\eta)}$. Their average truncation error obeys
$$\mathbb E\|\epsilon_{X^n}-\xi_{X^n}\|_1\le\zeta_n:=\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n}.$$
Indeed the conditional projector commutes with its state, so its trace-norm loss equals its failure probability. Its subnormalized output $A$ satisfies $0\preceq A\preceq\epsilon_{x^n}$, and the global-projection loss is at most $2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)A]}\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)\epsilon_{x^n}]}$. The subnormalized gentle estimate follows by applying the normalized lemma to $A/\operatorname{tr}A$ and multiplying back (the zero operator is immediate). Jensen gives the stated averaged bound.

For the $L_n$ independent words of a fixed message, centered Hilbert–Schmidt variance gives
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\left[\left(\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right)^2\right]
=\frac1{L_n}\{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\xi_{X^n}^2)-\operatorname{tr}(\theta^2)\}
\le\frac{e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}}{L_n}.$$
All cross terms have zero expectation by independence. The difference is supported in $P$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen imply
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}}.$$
Together with $\|\theta-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\|_1\le\zeta_n$, this proves
$$\mathbb E\left\|\tau_{m,n}-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\right\|_1\le2\zeta_n+\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}},\qquad\tau_{m,n}=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n}).$$
The right side decays exponentially and is independent of $m$. Consequently the expectation of the sum of average decoding error and average half-trace distance from this target decays exponentially. The codebook sample space is finite, so order the finite word/codebook alphabet and select its first deterministic codebook whose sum is at most twice its expectation (or zero if that expectation vanishes). This defines a sequence without countable choices. For that codebook let $a_n=M_n^{-1}\sum_m T(\tau_{m,n},\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n})$. The proved quantitative entropy estimate yields
$$\ell_n\le2a_n n\ln\dim E+2g(a_n)\longrightarrow0.$$
This establishes the required unnormalized Holevo strong secrecy; a mere limit of trace distance without this dimension/error-rate estimate would not suffice. The average decoding error also tends to zero, while $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$. If the ensemble's private information is nonpositive it gives no positive lower bound; rate zero remains achievable with one message.

newHelpers.title: Flat-input entanglement-assisted achievability by Weyl coding
newHelpers.statement: Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. The code consists of finite Weyl operations followed by a collective output/reference POVM; it has rate tending to $R$.
newHelpers.proof:
Fix a $D$-dimensional subspace of the input, with embedding $J$ and flat state $\tau=JJ^*/D$. Share $|\Phi_D\rangle$ between the sender's subspace and a receiver reference $R$. On the sender half apply the $D^2$ Weyl unitaries, each uniformly likely, before the input embedding. The Weyl matrices in the fixed ordered basis are $U_{ab}|j\rangle=e^{2\pi i bj/D}|j+a\pmod D\rangle$. Direct summation over $b$ kills off-diagonal matrix units; summation over $a$ gives the maximally mixed diagonal. Consequently their average action on the sender half of $\Phi_D$ gives $I_D/D\otimes I_R/D$.

Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the joint output on $B R$ of this finite cq alphabet through $\mathcal N$. Because $(U_{ab}\otimes I)|\Phi_D\rangle=(I\otimes U_{ab}^T)|\Phi_D\rangle$ in coefficient coordinates, all $\sigma_{ab}$ are related by a unitary on $R$ and have identical entropy $S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$ by purity of the full Stinespring output. Their average is $\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D$. Thus the ensemble Holevo information is exactly
$$\chi=\ln D+S(\mathcal N(\tau))-S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))=f_{\mathcal N}(\tau).$$
The actual accepted HSW theorem applies to this fixed finite cq channel $ab\mapsto\sigma_{ab}$, with output $B R$. Each cq codeword is physically implemented by its sequence of Weyl operations on independent shared maximally entangled pairs. Its collective POVM is a permitted receiver measurement and its rate/error are exactly those of HSW. Therefore every nonnegative rate strictly below $f_{\mathcal N}(\tau)$ is entanglement-assisted achievable. Dimension $D=1$ is included: the one-letter ensemble then has Holevo information zero.

newHelpers.title: Every finite extension is obtained from a purification by a channel
newHelpers.statement: Let $\omega_{ZA}$ be any finite-dimensional extension of $\rho_A$, and let $|\psi\rangle_{RA}$ purify $\rho_A$ with $R$ a copy of $A$. There is a CPTP map $\Lambda:R\to Z$ with $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(\psi)=\omega$.
newHelpers.proof: Purify $\omega$ on $ZAF$ and reorder to $A(ZF)$. In an eigenbasis of the positive part of $\rho_A$, the two purifications have the same Schmidt coefficients. Send each corresponding Schmidt vector of $R$ isometrically to its partner in $ZF$. Enlarge $F$ by a finite pure ancilla if necessary so this partial isometry extends to an isometry on all of $R$; the remaining orthonormal basis vectors are sent to unused orthonormal vectors. Taking the partial trace of that isometric output over $F$ defines the desired channel. Its action on the fixed purification is the chosen purification of $\omega$. This also covers singular $\rho_A$, since the zero-Schmidt directions never occur in $\psi$.
